How it works

A skill, a crew that knows your name, and a path into paid work.

PictureThis Production trains young people aged 16 to 29 in sound, cameras, lighting and streaming, then puts them on real crews with a working technician as a mentor.

  1. 01

    Train

    Eight Saturdays on sound, cameras, lighting and streaming. Hands on the gear from the first morning.

  2. 02

    Crew

    From week three you are on a real crew at Faithfire Production or a partner venue — supervised, but real.

  3. 03

    Mentor

    Monthly one-to-one check-ins with a working technician, and a reference from people the industry knows.

Why we exist

A working trade, taught properly.

Every week, churches, concert halls, hotels and conference centres across the GTA pay technicians to run sound, video and lighting. We teach the craft and the conduct — both are the job. A different offer than the street makes.

Our vision

A Toronto where young people build their future together, not on the streets, but as a crew: learning skills, earning a living, and looking out for one another.

Our mission

Free, hands-on training and mentorship in live production, on real shows alongside working technicians. Participants leave with a trade, a reference, and a path into paid work.

Programs

The eight-week course.

Eight weeks, taken together. Everyone starts at week 1. Nobody is behind. Training runs at 139 Millwick Dr and partner venues across the GTA.

01

Cables, connectors and signal flow

Coil, tape and test every cable type we own. Follow a signal from microphone to speaker and find the break we hid in it.

02

Digital consoles: the Wing and X32

Build a show file from empty: inputs, gains, EQ, routing, scenes. The two consoles most GTA rooms actually run.

03

Mixing a live band

Soundcheck a real band at Faithfire. Vocals first, then everything else. Learn what to do when it feeds back anyway.

04

Cameras and video switching (ATEM)

Frame, focus and follow. Then sit in the director’s chair and call a two-camera rehearsal on comms.

05

Lighting: rigging safely, running a desk

Hang, focus and cable a rig without hurting anyone. Program cues and run a service from the lighting desk.

06

Streaming, lyrics and media

Build a full ProPresenter service file: lyrics, scripture, sermon slides, stream output. Advance it live, on the director’s call.

07

Show calling, comms and event etiquette

Call a show start to finish. Comms discipline, dress codes, client manners — the conduct half of the job.

08

Capstone: crew a real production

A full event, crewed entirely by the cohort, mentors on comms only if needed. This is the reference you graduate with.

Mentoring

One-to-one, with a working technician.

Monthly check-ins. All mentors are police-checked and meet participants in crew spaces, never alone off-site.

Pathway · Production management

Run the whole show.

Advancing the event, building the run sheet and call sheets, managing the budget, and calling the show on the day.

Pathway · Technical management

Lead the department.

Planning the rig, choosing and maintaining the gear, signing off on safety, and teaching the next cohort.

Safeguarding · Our standards

We don’t promise jobs. We promise hours on real gear, a reference, and a crew that will say your name when a call comes in.

  • Every mentor passes a Vulnerable Sector Check before working with participants and follows a written code of conduct.
  • Mentors and participants meet in crew spaces, never alone off-site.
  • Participants aged 16 and 17 join with a parent or guardian’s consent.
  • Photos and recordings of participants are used only with consent, which can be withdrawn at any time.
  • The program is free, and it stays free. No fees, no gear purchases, no paid upsells.

Our vision · Free training and mentoring / Ages 16–29

PictureThis Production gives young people ages 16 to 29 free, hands-on training and mentorship in live production, in sound, cameras, lighting, and streaming, on real shows alongside working technicians. They leave with a trade, a reference, and a path into paid work.

PictureThis Production started with working technicians who kept meeting the same person: a young person with talent and no way in. No gear, no connections, no one to show them how a show actually runs. So we opened the room. PictureThis is the nonprofit that handles the training and mentoring. Faithfire Production, our production arm, is where the learning happens: real services, real events, real audiences, with participants working alongside the technicians who do this every week.

The next cohort starts in January: twenty places, eight weeks, free. Participants shadow, then assist, then run positions on real productions, paired with a mentor the whole way. Graduates go where the work is: church production teams, corporate AV crews, concert and event calls across the GTA.

An eight-week course, Saturdays 10:00 AM to 2:00 PM, at Faithfire Production, 139 Millwick Dr, and partner venues across the GTA. Cables and signal flow in week 1; a full production crewed by the cohort in week 8.

Every participant is paired with a working technician: someone who mixed, switched or lit a show this month. Monthly check-ins at minimum, help with first bookings, rates, and when to say no.

First bookings are usually cable and stagehand calls, then operating positions. We don't promise you a job. We promise hands-on time with real gear, honest instruction, a reference from people the industry knows, and a crew that'll say your name when a call comes in.

The other half of putting on a show: advancing the event, building the run sheet and call sheets, managing the budget, and calling the show on the day. Participants who work well on a crew learn to run the production, not just handle one role in it.

For those who go on to lead a department: planning the rig, choosing and maintaining the gear, signing off on safety, and teaching the next cohort. It's the top of the pathway, the people who spec out the room and are accountable for it.

Participants aged 16 and 17 join with a parent or guardian's consent, and a parent or guardian can reach the program lead at any time.

Photos and recordings of participants are used only with consent, and consent can be withdrawn.

The first cohort wasn't a class. It was a crew. Faithfire Production is where PictureThis got its start: a church production team at 139 Millwick Dr that grew into a full production department, one show at a time. Most of the crew started with little to no experience. They learned the way this program teaches today: by shadowing someone more experienced, helping out on real shows, and then running their own positions.

These days, that crew handles two Sunday services plus events like Cue & A and Revival Hub, and other churches and production teams specifically request them. They're also the go-to mentors for everyone who comes after them: the folks teaching cables in week 1 are the same ones who learned it all in that very room.

That's the integration, plain and simple: PictureThis is the nonprofit behind the mission, the training, and the standards. Faithfire is its production arm, and its first success story. Every new cohort learns inside a real, working production company, not a simulation.

As the year ends, I've been promoted to Crew Chief, and I'm excited and grateful. It's another step in my growth, and I'm looking forward to the responsibility: to keep learning, to lead well, and to support this team the way it supported me."
